content:
I've recently been doing some work (#38963, merged), #39233 (actively in discussion) moving things from the Pi namespace into the Functionnamespace, with the hope that in future these become more usable with dot notation, even in the dependent case. @Eric Wieser has encouraged me to initiate a general discussion about this.

Essentially there is a large tangle of different approaches to Pi and Function, and it's hard to get a sense for what the consistent name for many of these operations should be. Function.prod feels like the right choice to me because it's the Function analogue of LinearMap.prod etc., but as now defined it also works in the dependent case. You might think "Function = non-dependent, Pi = dependent", but we have things like Function.swap - why isn't this Pi.swap? I agree it should be Function.swap but I find myself struggle to explain why. There certainly are places where we use the old Π notation, and conceptually speaking it is more clearly linked to a product, by analogy with the notation for Sigma. There are times when we are clearly thinking of Pi as "a product with arbitrarily indexed components" - Pi.instAdd is a great example of this - and then there are times when it seems more like we are thinking of it as a function, i.e. the language, at least, that we use to describe Pi.single (though equally one can view this as an arbitrary product). Conversely you have things like Function.eval which are distinctly defined in the dependent case but, in my view, actually have more meaning under the "arbitrary product" interpretation which seems closer to what we mean by Pi. I find myself unable to identify at all what the criteria is for Function versus Pi in namespace terms.

I would like to start a discussion on what we feels our general approach should be. One wild idea I had was that you could choose to make Pi a one-element structure (in the special case where it is indexed by a type etc., i.e. we're genuinely dealing with data, it matches Sigma etc. and I think it probably gives cleaner behaviour):

structure Pi {ι : Type*} (α : ι → Type*) where toFun : (i : ι) → α i

namespace Pi

variable {ι : Type*} {α β : ι → Type*}

protected def map (f : ∀ i, α i → β i) (p : Pi α) : Pi β := Pi.mk (fun i ↦ f i (p.toFun i))

@[simp]
lemma map_apply (f : ∀ i, α i → β i) (a : Pi α) (i : ι) :
    (Pi.map f a).toFun i = f i (a.toFun i) := rfl

end Pi

Under this way of thinking, we would use Pi (for which we could use the Π notation) when what we mean is, distinctly, an arbitrarily-indexed product - and clearly this admits dot notation easily, which is nice - and retain Function for things like, say, Function.decomp, where imo a function-view interpretation is cleanest.

But even if you don't like this wild idea - and I think it IS wild - I do think the general situation is confusing and I want to start that conversation.

moving things from the Function namespace into the Pinamespace

Did you mean the other way around (Pi namespace into the Function namespace)?

You've already started moving from the Pi into the Function namespace (Pi.prod -> Function.prod), so I don't see why we shouldn't continue this way.

What I will say is that I don't like writing f : ∀ i, α i → β i, since it's really f : (i : _) → α i → β i or f : Π i, α i → β i. I think ∀ should only be used for propositions and not functions.
I did mean this! I also agree with you that ∀ i, α i → β i is somehow morally unclean, though in some ways this is more of a core issue.
f : (i : _) → α i → β i is the way I think.

Mentioned it in #39233, but I think it might be reasonable to maintain piMap as the general name for things of thePi.map shape. Like - moving Pi.map to Function.piMap makes sense to me.

In a similar way, things like docs#Pi.constAddHom could become AddHom.const.
This being said I'm also happy with Function.map - but if we do that I think all the piMaps need changing to map
I like Function.piMap more than Function.map. If we do change that, then shouldn't docs#Function.prod be Function.piProd as well?

Well, .prod is the more usual thing there. actually there's a slightly odd thing where Prod.map is generally .prodMap in other namespaces - again see docs#AddHom.prod and docs#AddHom.prodMap.

I think Prod.map is a fine name but, arguably, we should also have Function.prodMap as an alternative name for it, to be consistent. Of course Prod can also on some level be viewed as a pi type with the index type being Bool or Fin 2, and in that perspective, Prod.map is actually also Pi.map - hence the original name there.

I guess, in general, Pi is the appropriate namespace when you are considering (i : _) → α i as the generalisation of tuples, and Function is the appropriate namespace when you're considering it as, well, a function.
Like, docs#Pi.group is about Pi-as-tuple I would argue, and Pi as a namespace maybe makes sense there.

And under this interpretation, I do think Pi.map makes some sense as the generalisation of Prod.map. Equally though I think Function.piMap makes sense! I suppose just as I think Prod.map and Function.prodMap are both sensible names (and so possibly we should have both), Function.piMap and Pi.map are both reasonably sensible...

Now, one option would be to make Pi α into a one-field structure which contains a (i : _) → α i. It would be this structure that would be equipped with things like the instances of Group etc. It would have a FunLike instance too. Separately though you might still want instances on the raw function type... but the goal would be a semantic separation between "Pi-as-tuple" and "Pi-as-function".

Wrenna Robson said:

Well, .prod is the more usual thing there. actually there's a slightly odd thing where Prod.map is generally .prodMap in other namespaces

This is how the naming rules say to turn Foo.bar into a token in a longer name.
Aye, which somewhat makes sense but I would argue makes the Function case weird!
